extracted.intended_audience: hospital coders, health system administrators, device manufacturers, clinical coders, Medicare payment policy stakeholders, and members of the public submitting comments on IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria used by CMS in the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule to determine MS-DRG logic changes, creation/deletion of base MS-DRGs, severity-level reassignment of procedure codes, O.R./non-O.R. designations, and title wording updates. Includes the quantitative and qualitative tests applied to claims data to justify grouping or subgroup splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five criteria to create subgroups (split a base MS-DRG)
rubrics_metrics.description: All five criteria must be met for a base MS-DRG to be split (or subdivided) by a CC subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the proposed new MS-DRGs to identify cases reporting a PJI with a hip or knee procedure with or without procedure code XW0V0P7, there is at least (1) 500 cases in the MCC group and 500 cases in the without MCC group; (2) 5 percent of the cases in the MCC group and 5 percent in the without MCC group; (3) a 20 percent difference in average costs between the MCC group and the without MCC group; (4) a $2,000 difference in average costs between the MCC group and the without MCC group; and (5) a 3-percent reduction in cost variance, indicating that the proposed severity level splits increase the explanatory power of the base MS-DRG in capturing differences in expected cost between the proposed MS-DRG severity level splits by at least 3-percent and thus improve the overall accuracy of the IPPS payment system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply three-way then two-way split process
rubrics_metrics.description: If criteria for a three-way split fail, the next step is to determine if the criteria are satisfied for a two-way split.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As discussed in section II.C.1.b. of the preamble, CMS first evaluates a three-way split; if that fails (for example, failed to meet the criterion of at least a 20% difference in average costs in the without CC/MCC group), CMS then evaluates two-way splits (e.g., with MCC vs without MCC or with CC/MCC vs without CC/MCC) against the established subgroup criteria. Tables in the rule illustrate when three-way or two-way splits fail (e.g., failing to meet 500 cases in the MCC group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evidence for reassignment: average length of stay and average costs alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reassign procedure codes or cases between severity levels or MS-DRGs when average length of stay (LOS) and average costs for those cases are generally comparable to or more aligned with the higher severity level or other MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS compared average LOS and average costs of cases reporting a principal diagnosis of PJI with hip/knee procedure or reporting procedure code XW0V0P7 against averages for their respective MS-DRGs. Where cases at a lower severity level had average costs/LOS aligned with higher severity MS-DRGs, CMS proposed reassignment (example: reassignment of XW0V0P7 from lower severity to higher MCC level in several MDCs). Specific observations (e.g., 3,262 cases in MS-DRG 463 had costs ~$49 less than the MS-DRG average) were used to support decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GROUPER logic, surgical hierarchy, and restriction/cluster logic for case assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Case grouping is determined by the ICD-10 MS-DRG GROUPER logic, including listed diagnosis and procedure code lists, surgical hierarchy, code clusters, and any restriction logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS analyzed how removal of restriction logic (e.g., in MS-DRGs 466–468 and 485–487) would redistribute cases across MS-DRGs under the proposed Version 44 GROUPER logic and surgical hierarchy. Examples: procedure code 0SP90JZ was listed both in logic for MS-DRGs 463–465 and as part of a cluster with 0SR9019 for MS-DRGs 466–468; removal of cluster restriction caused cases with 0SP90JZ to group to 463–465. CMS refers to the ICD-10 MS-DRG Definitions Manual for complete GROUPER logic documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove restriction logic and delete/create MS-DRGs when subgroup criteria not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after applying the GROUPER and subgroup criteria, existing MS-DRGs no longer meet subgroup/split criteria, CMS may delete those MS-DRGs and create new base MS-DRGs with revised logic lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposed to delete MS-DRGs 466–468 and 485–487 after finding they would no longer satisfy criteria for a 3-way split following removal of restriction logic, and to create new base MS-DRG 449 (Revision of Hip or Knee Replacement) and new base MS-DRG 400 (Knee Procedures with Principal Diagnosis of Infection). CMS provided simulated tables and proposed logic lists (Tables 6P.3c/6P.3d) to reflect these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: O.R. vs non-O.R. procedure designation changes based on data and MS-DRG assignment impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Redesignate a procedure code's O.R./non-O.R. status when data show reassignment of cases and a change in group assignment that would be better reflected by a different designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposed to redesignate procedure code XW0V0P7 (currently designated non-O.R.) in order to affect MS-DRG assignment at the higher with MCC severity level for specified MS-DRGs, because analysis showed cases reporting XW0V0P7 without PJI were reassigned from lower to higher severity levels and that cases reporting both PJI and XW0V0P7 had longer LOS and higher costs. The designation change is proposed to ensure those cases are reassigned at the highest severity level consistent with other assignment proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title wording must reflect logical grouping ('or' vs 'and')
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRG titles should accurately reflect the logic for case assignment; use 'or' when the logic is satisfied by either of the listed procedures rather than implying both are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS noted that titles for MS-DRGs 463, 464, and 465 contain 'Wound Debridement and Skin Graft Except Hand…' which may mislead by implying both procedures are required. CMS proposed to revise 'and' to 'or' because GROUPER logic is satisfied when either a wound debridement or a skin graft (except hand) procedure code from the logic list is reported. Title changes are reflected in test GROUPER Software Version 44 and draft Definitions Manual Version 44.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider clinical coherence and similarity of indications/resource use when grouping procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Group procedures and cases in MS-DRGs based on demonstrated clinical similarity, indications, patient populations, and resource utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS concluded that pancreatic islet cell transplantation cases are clinically coherent with pancreas transplant cases given similar indications, patient populations, and goals (glycemic management, immunosuppression), and therefore should be grouped with pancreas transplant procedures for clinical coherence despite technical differences. The MS-DRG system seeks to group diagnoses and procedures with similar clinical characteristics and utilization of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review predecessor code assignments and multiple relevant factors in assigning new/revised procedure codes
rubrics_metrics.description: When finalizing new or revised procedure code assignments, CMS reviews predecessor MS-DRG assignments and considers severity of illness, treatment difficulty, complexity of service, and resources used in diagnosis/treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The established process includes initially reviewing predecessor code MS-DRG assignment and designation while considering other relevant factors (for example, severity of illness, treatment difficulty, complexity of service and the resources utilized in the diagnosis and/or treatment of the condition). If new/revised procedure code proposals are finalized after the Spring update, they are footnoted in the final rule tables; the public may provide feedback on finalized assignments which CMS considers for the following fiscal year.
